title: Pop Culture Digest — Saturday, October 24, 2026
description:
Saturday · October 24, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Saturday’s conversation: DC’s Clayface heading for a No. 1 opening, the final James Bond screen tests reportedly happening in London this weekend, Jay-Z bringing Blue Ivy out at SoFi Stadium, and Drake singing with the Backstreet Boys at his 40th birthday party.
Movies

Clayface is on track for a No. 1 opening, with the Nathan Fielder doc close behind

Warner Bros. and DC’s R-rated body-horror movie made an estimated $9.5 million Friday, including $3.5 million from Thursday previews, and Deadline projects a $23–25 million opening at 3,458 theaters. That’s a solid start for a film that cost about $44 million, in line with Smile ($22.6 million), and audiences like it: 93% on Rotten Tomatoes’ audience score and 76% with critics.

The race isn’t settled. A24’s You Can See Everything, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary, expanded to 2,655 theaters and made $5.8 million Friday, up 5% from its opening day. Deadline sees $19 million or more, which would make it bigger in its second weekend than its first. Laika’s Wildwood is third at about $11 million, while Taika Waititi’s Klara and the Sun is struggling at under $1 million.

Clayface trailer on YouTube →   ·   Deadline →

Movies

The final James Bond screen tests are reportedly happening this weekend

Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor are among three to five actors reportedly doing final auditions for 007 in London, according to the Hollywood Reporter, Deadline and Variety. The tests have three parts: stunts, camera presence and dialogue. Variety says Slow Horses star Lowden may be edging ahead, and Jacob Elordi is reportedly not testing.

No official trailer or announcement exists yet. Amazon MGM hasn’t commented, Deadline says there’s no timeline for a decision even after tests wrap, and producer Amy Pascal has called the end of the year “a good bet.” Denis Villeneuve is directing from a Steven Knight script, with the film reportedly due in 2028.

BBC News →

Music

Jay-Z brings out Blue Ivy and Scarface at SoFi, fueling Super Bowl halftime talk

The first of two “Jay-Z 30” shows at Inglewood’s SoFi Stadium ran two hours and more than 30 songs, from “Hovi Baby” and “Izzo (H.O.V.A.)” to “Empire State of Mind.” Blue Ivy Carter played keys on “The Story of O.J.” and “Dead Presidents,” Scarface came out for a rare “This Can’t Be Life,” and John Legend and DJ Khaled closed the night with “God Did.” Fans also spotted Beyoncé, Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams together in a suite.

SoFi is where the February 2027 Super Bowl will be played, and with talk that Jay may be the halftime performer, Variety called the show a possible test run. Tonight is the final night of the anniversary tour, and big surprises are expected.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Variety →

Celebrities

Drake turns 40 with the Backstreet Boys, Hermès bags and a $1 million game show

Drake celebrated at New York’s Casa Cipriani Friday night, hours before his birthday today. The Backstreet Boys performed and he joined them for “I Want It That Way,” the song he has said played at his bar mitzvah. TMZ reports guests got Chanel and Hermès handbags, and a game show offered cash prizes up to $1 million. “Tonight isn’t about a tour, an album release, or a bunch of videos we shot,” he told the room. “It’s about being alive, staying alive.”

The same day, the RIAA gave him 30 new certifications, making him the first artist to pass 350 million certified units. Views, “In My Feelings” and “Marvin’s Room” went Diamond, and he now holds a record 18 Diamond plaques.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Billboard →

Bottom of the news

  • Zendaya will campaign for a best actress Oscar nomination for Dune: Part Three, out Dec. 18; it would be her first.
  • Meghan said she is “deeply distressed” by reports that child abuse images were found at her father Thomas Markle’s former home; he denies the claims.
  • Anderson .Paak and Cordae released their joint album Heavy Is the Crown, and Michael Kiwanuka put out his long-delayed fifth album, FUDGE.
  • John Legend released Muse, produced and co-written by Pharrell, and John Mayer dropped “Tom and Jerry,” his first solo single in five years.
  • Amy Winehouse’s Back to Black and My Chemical Romance’s The Black Parade got 20th-anniversary reissues with unreleased material.
  • Black Bear’s Olivia Colman comedy Wicker is heading for a strong $6 million-plus start, with 93% from critics.
  • Val Chmerkovskiy is back at Dancing With the Stars rehearsals after his one-week suspension over a post about Carrie Ann Inaba.
